plausibility.question: P1 gravity
plausibility.answer: Foot on the OD-C01 floor plane y 40 (+Y down); OD-H01 centroid (-0.067, -0.872, 7.232) lies over the saddle span z -3.0..31.0 (10.23 inside rib 1's front face, 23.77 inside rib 2's rear face); load path saddle, web, foot, four M3 screws.

plausibility.question: P2 function chains
plausibility.answer: Tie path connected: slots 6.0 x 2.5 at y 7 on z 17 and 28 pass a 4.8 x 1.4 tie beyond the -Y features (z <= 13.6); the tie drops through the 2.30 / 2.65 post-to-plate gaps and crosses the plate corners at r 31.66 / 31.36 (A-07, F2).

plausibility.question: P3 moving parts
plausibility.answer: No moving part; the vibrating pump keeps 2.300 to the -X post, 2.650 +X, 2.788 to both ribs; lowered along +Y from 60 mm it keeps >= 2.300 and 0.0 mm3, the sleeve touching only at the final pose.

plausibility.question: P4 human factors
plausibility.answer: The pump (x -27.20..26.85) drops between post faces 59.0 apart; the four holes are open from above; the nearest post corner is 4.03 from each rear hole axis, so an M3 head (r 2.75) and a driver shaft clear it.

plausibility.question: P5 absurdity
plausibility.answer: An 80 x 52 x 40 mm, 32.3 g PETG two-saddle cradle for a 0.5 kg vibratory pump on a rubber sleeve is in proportion with OEM pump brackets.

plausibility.question: P6 floating, embedded, mirrored, upside-down
plausibility.answer: One solid standing on its foot, saddle faces toward the pump (-Y), in the spec frame (OD-H01 in the assembly equals the input); the cradle is not embedded in anything. The assumed sleeve solid shares 1427.17 mm3 with OD-H01 (F6), an A-03 model limit outside the cradle.

findings.required: Soft: no unacceptable vibration to the chassis with the OEM sleeve fitted (bench)
findings.risk_basis: a bench gate no geometric check can answer; the rubber path rests on A-03 and A-05, and the ties also bear on the steel side plates (F2), a path around the sleeve
findings.fix_direction: bench-test the first print with the OEM sleeve and ties fitted; add a rubber pad under the tie at the plate corners if it buzzes

findings.required: the tie rides on the sleeve (spec section 4 C1)
findings.at: side plate corners (-27.20, -16.20) r 31.66 and (26.85, -16.20) r 31.36, over the tie bands z 14.6..19.4 and 25.6..30.4
findings.risk_basis: the modelled sleeve (A-03) stops at |x| 23.5, so between the post slots and the sleeve the tie crosses bare steel plate corners; A-07 assumes the real sleeve covers them; a sheet edge can chafe the tie and carry vibration around the rubber
findings.fix_direction: confirm on OD-H02 (scan or calipers); if the plates are bare, route the tie under the saddle or add a pad at the corners

findings.required: clearance = 0 on the saddle arcs, interference <= 0
findings.risk_basis: the zero gap holds only at r 26.650 exactly (controls: r 26.75 gives a 0.100 gap, r 26.55 on one arc 26.41 mm3); FDM holds about +-0.1..0.2; the coil under the saddles reads r 23.58..23.86 against the sleeve ID radius 23.65, so a real tube sleeve would stand up to 0.21 proud at theta 135 and 0.07 shy at theta 45
findings.fix_direction: retire A-03 with OD-H02 calipers; restate REQ-04 as a banded squeeze the rubber tolerates (for example 0.0..0.3 radial)

findings.at: (-29.500, 0.000, 12.0..33.0) -X post inner face to the -X side plate x -27.20

least_sure_answers.answer: Confirmed: 6.9e-13 on each rib, 0.0 mm3; rib 1's front face z -3.000 is 3.0 inside the sleeve end z -6.0; the coil under the saddles reads r 23.58..23.86 against the sleeve ID 23.65, so the fit is uncertain by about 0.2 either way. Rated F3 MEDIUM.
